name: pcap_summary
description: Read a pcap or pcapng with no external dependency and return a census of it: the format and version, an interface table (link type, snap length and time resolution per interface), the pcapng interface statistics blocks (the capturing interface's own drop counters, when the file carries them), the time range (exact to the capture's own tick, raw value beside it; duration_ns is exact), tuple aggregates or endpoint aggregates with bytes_original and bytes_captured kept apart, top talkers and ports, SYN observations (syn_observations counts SYN-only packets; syn_unique counts SYN events: a SYN sent again with the same sequence number within 120 seconds of the first of its event is folded into it and counted in syn_folded, and a row keeps at most 10,000 events, after which syn_unique is a lower bound), and the truncation each packet really had (captured shorter than on the wire, by protocol, and the payload bytes that survived). Not measured: TCP connections or sessions (a tuple used again later merges with its earlier use, and a SYN says nothing about a completed handshake), application data delivered, UDP/QUIC or persistent connections as events, packet loss in a classic pcap, the correctness of the capture clock. Blocks of unsupported types, malformed options and frames that are not IP are counted, never dropped silently. A capture that is cut off or corrupt is summarised up to the damage and says so (status partial, capture_read_to_the_end false, stopped_reading naming the packets read, the byte it stopped at and why): the summary covers the packets before that point and nothing after it. A pcapng block this tool does not decode (name resolution, decryption secrets, custom, unknown) is measured and skipped, never read, however long it is; a block it reads whole is held to a packet's size plus its options (an options block to 1 MiB), and a longer one ends the read there. Classic records whose fraction field is a second or more, and records that hold more bytes than the snap length allows, are counted. Aggregates spill to SQLite past max_memory_tuples, so memory does not follow the capture; the whole result is kept on disk and named when a page is shorter. A host or port filter applies to the rows, the top lists, the protocol counts and the SYN counts, not to the whole-capture totals (filtered.applies_to says so). top_talkers counts an address as the SOURCE of a packet, top_ports the DESTINATION port. The link-type field's FCS bits are read apart from the type, a pcapng section's hardware, OS and application and an interface's drop counts (statistics blocks and packet-block drop counts) are reported, and stacked VLAN tags (802.1ad, 0x9100) are followed. The text a capture says about its capturing machine and interfaces (hardware, OS, application, an interface's name, description, OS and capture filter) is capture-supplied text and is printed through the same withholding block as the other tools of the pack: readable text stays, a token-shaped run does not. The tool keeps its own clock (max_seconds, default 540, at most 570; the manifest's limit is 600): when it runs out the packets read so far are summarised and the answer is partial. The ordering and writing of the lists after the reading end 15 seconds before the manifest's limit whatever max_seconds was: past that the rows stop, the answer is partial and listing_cut_by_its_own_clock says how many were written of how many. With group endpoint, the summing of the tuples into endpoints is under the same end: if it does not finish no endpoint row is listed (a sum over some tuples is not an endpoint's sum), and listing_cut_by_its_own_clock.endpoint_aggregation says how many tuples were summed of how many. Interfaces, interface statistics and section options are shown fifty at a time (the others are counted, said in a note, and all of them are in a file the answer names), and a pcapng with more than 10,000 of any of them is read to that point only (partial). Every answer carries status (complete, partial or failed) and status_basis; exit 0 means the engine ran, and a refusal is JSON and exit 1. SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP remove the temporary aggregate file, print partial JSON and exit 128 plus the signal.

path.description: A classic pcap or a pcapng file (not a pcapng compressed or packed in another container)

top.description: Rows shown inline per table (default 200). When more exist the whole table is written as JSON Lines under $OUT/tool-output (work/<agent>/tool-output outside a job) and named in pages.<table>.all_results

host.description: Only aggregates involving this address, written in any form (IPv6 is compared as an address, not as text)

out_dir.description: Optional empty directory under work/ (in a job, under $OUT; work/<your agent id>/name is mapped to $OUT/name) for the complete tuple_conversations.tsv or endpoint_aggregates.tsv. The temporary aggregate file is removed on every way out

with_syn_times.description: Include the time of each SYN event on each aggregate, for beacon_score (with_starts is accepted as an old name and noted in the answer). They are SYN events, not connection starts: a SYN sent again within 120 seconds of the first of its event is folded into it. Inline a row shows the first 100 times; the whole list is in syn_times_file and in the TSV

group.description: tuple (default; session is the old name for it): one row per sorted pair of (address, port) and protocol; endpoint: one row per pair of addresses and a service port, the port taken from a SYN or a SYN/ACK, or guessed (service_port_basis says which)

max_memory_tuples.description: Aggregates kept in memory before they move to a temporary SQLite file (default 200000); the answer says spilled_to_disk

max_seconds.description: The tool's own clock for reading the capture, from 1 to 570 seconds (default 540). When it runs out the packets read so far are summarised and the answer is partial (stopped_reading.kind is time_limit)
